purpose: Separate runtime-state optimization from persistence-format choice for CPO masks.

torch_save_measurement.support_layout: first k positions; serialization-size test only

interpretation: Rank-local sparse idx/ref is still attractive for steady-state runtime because each rank keeps only its partition slice.
Global int64-sparse persistence is only smaller than the public dense-bool+fp32-ref format below 12.5% support; after union growth it can become substantially larger.

For tensors with numel < 2^31, int32 persistence moves the dense-bool crossover to 25%, but it still loses after enough union growth and must be widened or otherwise adapted before indexing if the execution path requires int64 indices.

Bit-packing the global mask while retaining fp32 references is smaller than both sparse formats at the tested 10%-34.39% supports; load-time conversion to sorted rank-local indices should therefore be evaluated as a hybrid persistence/runtime design.
These are storage-format results, not training-quality results and not real Qwen task_k.pt measurements.
